segments.name: Tools & Outdoor
segments.description: Worldwide leader in hand tools, power tools, outdoor products and related accessories sold to professional end users, distributors, dealers, retail consumers and industrial customers.
segments.evidence: The Tools & Outdoor segment is comprised of the Power Tools Group ("PTG"), Hand Tools, Accessories & Storage ("HTAS"), and Outdoor Power Equipment ("Outdoor") product lines.

segments.name: Engineered Fastening
products: drawn arc weld studs and systems
segments.description: Global leader of highly engineered, application-based fastening components sold to automotive, manufacturing, electronics, construction and aerospace customers.
segments.evidence: The business primarily sells highly engineered components such as fasteners, fittings and various engineered products, which are designed for specific applications across multiple verticals.

revenueModel.text: The Company earns revenue from selling tools, outdoor products and engineered fastening components, largely through retailers, home centers, mass merchants, distributors, dealers and a direct sales force.
revenueModel.evidence: The majority of sales are distributed through retailers, including home centers, mass merchants, hardware stores, and retail lumber yards, as well as third-party distributors, independent dealers, and a direct sales force.

changes.text: In the first quarter of 2025, the Industrial segment was renamed Engineered Fastening.
changes.evidence: In the first quarter of 2025, the Industrial segment was renamed "Engineered Fastening" as a result of a more focused portfolio following recent divestitures.

changes.text: In April 2024, the Company sold its Infrastructure business, comprised of the attachment and handheld hydraulic tools business.
changes.evidence: In April 2024, the Company sold its Infrastructure business, comprised of the attachment and handheld hydraulic tools business, for net proceeds of $729 million.

changes.text: In December 2025, the Company announced a definitive agreement to sell its Consolidated Aerospace Manufacturing (CAM) business.
changes.evidence: Most recently, the Company announced in December 2025 that it had entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Consolidated Aerospace Manufacturing ("CAM") business for $1.8 billion in cash.
